findings.source_quote: ἐχάρη δὲ ὁ ποιμὴν ἐπὶ τούτοις, ὅτι πάντες ἠλλοιώθησαν καὶ ἀπέθεντο τὰς σχισμὰς αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: Retain each rod group, response conditions, renewed seal and plural spirits; select sinners with declared Athos and partial Michigan evidence.
findings.issue: The unit's theological metadata attributes content and textual decisions to this section that it does not contain. S.8.v describes rod groups, their changed condition, and the shepherd's rejoicing; it contains no renewed seal, plural spirits, or sinners-versus-sins selection. The supplied report locates the sinners selection in S.8.vi.6, not this unit. Likewise, the lexical entry “μετάνοια / διψυχεῖν” documents words absent from the selected source. This is misleading unit-level provenance, even though the reader text does not insert those claims.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace the theological metadata with a unit-specific account of the distinct rod groups, changed conditions, and editorial supplements. Remove or explicitly relocate the absent-word lexical entry and the seal, spirits, response-condition, and sinners-selection material to the relevant units. Any replacement metadata requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἐχάρη δὲ ὁ ποιμὴν ἐπὶ τούτοις, ὅτι πάντες ἠλλοιώθησαν καὶ ἀπέθεντο τὰς σχισμὰς αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: The shepherd rejoiced over them. They had all changed and put away their cracks.
findings.issue: The source explicitly makes their change and removal of cracks the reason for the shepherd's rejoicing. Separate statements leave that causal relationship implicit rather than translating ὅτι.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction: “The shepherd rejoiced over them because they had all changed and put away their cracks.” Review this replacement before adopting it.

findings.source_quote: εἶτα ἐπέδωκαν οἱ ἐλάχιστον ἔχοντες χλωρόν, τὰ δὲ λοιπὰ μέρη ξηρά
findings.english_quote: Next came the people whose rods had only a little green. The rest was dry.
findings.issue: The source says that this group handed in its rods. “Next came” replaces that action with arrival, and paragraph 6 never subsequently states that these people handed their rods in. Unlike the standard edition, the simplified edition therefore omits this group's submission.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction: “Then the people whose rods had only a little green handed them in. The rest of each rod was dry.” Review the replacement against the source before adoption.

findings.source_quote: ἐχάρη δὲ ὁ ποιμὴν ἐπὶ τούτοις, ὅτι πάντες ἠλλοιώθησαν καὶ ἀπέθεντο τὰς σχισμὰς αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: Retain each rod group, response conditions, renewed seal and plural spirits; select sinners with declared Athos and partial Michigan evidence.
findings.issue: Independently checked against S.8.v, this theological metadata describes material absent from the selected section. The sinners selection belongs to S.8.vi.6 in the supplied report. The lexical entry “μετάνοια / διψυχεῖν” also concerns absent words. Additionally, the simplification metadata claims to retain repentance conditions, a renewed seal, plural spirits, a sinners noun, and warnings that this section does not contain. These blocks misrepresent what this simplified unit translates and preserves.
findings.suggested_revision: Rewrite the theological and simplification metadata specifically for this unit's rod groups, fractions, changed conditions, rejoicing, and disclosed supplements. Remove or explicitly relocate the absent-word lexical entry and the material belonging to other sections. Submit replacement metadata for fresh review.

summary: The standard reader text covers the selected working source, but its unit-level metadata requires correction. The simplified edition independently requires correction of an omitted submission action, an implicit rather than explicit causal link, and mis-scoped metadata. Both editions disclose the bracketed supplements and retain the chosen longer working reading without treating the reported Michigan alternative as certification of that reconstruction. The supplied comparison reports were treated as attributed evidence, not authenticated manuscript inspection or exhaustive collation. Proposed corrections are not automatically approved.
